title: Rex Fleet Issue 2 Cover
summary: Sell the rescue that costs Venn her command: a crippled mixed Verge–Shard evacuation ship is dying under fire while Thunderbreak visibly turns away from the authorized relief convoy to save the people nobody has permission to save.
settingText: Space outside Auric near a broken-moon passage; Thunderbreak bridge foreground framing a crippled civilian evacuation ship, distant authorized relief convoy, and incoming hostile fire.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: Venn is visibly choosing the crippled civilian ship over the authorized mission. The reader should understand the fork in one glance before noticing any weapons.

CAMERA / FRAMING: portrait 35mm-equivalent view from just behind and to the right of Venn's command position, camera near shoulder height. Venn occupies the lower-left quarter in clear three-quarter profile, head and eyes turned toward the damaged evacuation ship. Do not center her and do not have her look at the reader.

PRIMARY FOCAL SHAPE: the crippled evacuation ship sits just below center, large enough that torn plating, improvised repairs and failing life-support light read immediately. It must look civilian and overburdened, not sleek or militarized.

SECONDARY STORY GEOMETRY: make the decision literal through two diverging movement vectors. Thunderbreak's projected turn / bridge sightline bends toward the evacuation ship. The authorized relief convoy recedes on the opposite upper-right vector. The reader should be able to trace both paths without reading interface text.
THREAT: incoming hostile fire enters from the far outer edge as two or three clean vectors, never as a wall of missiles. The danger should tighten the choice, not overwhelm it.

PERFORMANCE: Venn is still, upright and controlled. One hand may brace on the command rail or console. No clenched-fist hero pose, no grimacing, no cape-like coat motion. Her authority comes from the fact that everyone else is waiting for the course she chooses.

LIGHTING: cool Fleet bridge light on Venn; hot white-orange damage light from the refugee ship beyond; restrained red threat reflections. Verified route green appears only as navigation geometry or beacon state, never as an overall green wash.

TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: keep the entire canonical masthead/tagline field visually quiet enough to read cleanly. No face, weapon burst or critical ship silhouette may be hidden by REX FLEET. The evacuation ship's recognizable body should sit below the tagline line.

THUMBNAIL TEST: at phone size the image must still reduce to three readable facts—Venn in command, one wounded civilian ship, two diverging paths. If missiles, consoles or stars become the strongest shapes, simplify.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show Venn stripped of command, Abby turning on Billie, the hostage tug, the Crown Ring opening, or the final rescue outcome.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: command under moral pressure. The image is the instant before the consequence. The reader should ask, 'Is she really turning the ship?' rather than 'Who wins the battle?'

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: generic heroic captain portrait; Thunderbreak exterior glamour shot; equal-weight collage of Venn/Abby/Tess/refugees; giant explosion; readable tactical HUD text; refugee ship rendered as a warship; relief convoy omitted so there is no visible sacrifice.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 3 Cover
summary: Sell Auric's impossible morning-after problem: the luxury ring has rooms, but 'empty' does not mean unowned, safe, warm, or politically available.
settingText: Auric Crown Ring luxury residence corridor during a heat failure; ornate doorway, abandoned personal belongings, emergency refugee bedding and failing environmental light.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: one beautiful doorway contains two legitimate claims. The architecture itself should make 'vacant' and 'available' visibly different ideas.

CAMERA / FRAMING: nearly straight-on portrait view down the Crown Ring corridor with a tall apartment doorway centered slightly below mid-frame. Use a 28–32mm equivalent lens: enough depth to see corridor and room, but no fisheye distortion.

PRIMARY FOCAL SHAPE: the open door and its bright vertical frame. Inside the apartment, improvised refugee bedding, medicine, one child's blanket and visible cold breath occupy expensive flooring beneath a failing chandelier. Outside the threshold, preserved family possessions and one returning Auric resident establish prior ownership without requiring exposition.

HUMAN STAGING: keep one refugee just inside and one resident just outside, neither aggressive. Their bodies should angle toward the room, not toward each other like duelists. The question is who can live here, not who is morally correct.

ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRADICTION: luxury materials—polished metal, decorative trim, expensive wall surfaces—must coexist with portable heaters, temporary bedding and emergency light. The room should look valuable and unlivable at the same time.

LIGHTING: cold blue-white failing environmental light from the corridor; weak warmer emergency or heater light inside. Avoid sepia nostalgia. The visible temperature difference should be more important than decorative richness.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: use dark ceiling/corridor space behind the masthead. The door frame must remain fully legible below the tagline. Do not place faces in the top masthead field.
THUMBNAIL TEST: the cover must reduce to one tall glowing doorway with a person on each side. If the bedding and luxury detail are required to understand the image, the hierarchy is too weak.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show the sabotage culprit, Richard's evidence broadcast, Billie reaching the clinic, Tali's disappearance, the defense compact, or the ring's final survival state.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: shelter turning into politics. Make an apartment doorway feel as consequential as a battleship airlock.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: refugees presented as invaders; residents presented as cruel elites; warm cozy shelter; generic disaster hallway; property documents or explanatory signage; split-screen montage instead of one continuous doorway.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 4 Cover
summary: Sell the Tal Corvus evacuation as a road that is simultaneously an escape route and a firing line: civilians have already started moving, and every armed faction knows exactly where they must pass.
settingText: Tal Corvus evacuation route through a narrow certified corridor volume; civilian transports and families moving toward safety while Fleet and Shard forces close around the route.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: a single thin green road out, with armed power closing on both sides. Civilians must own the center of the image.

CAMERA / FRAMING: long portrait perspective looking directly down the evacuation axis, as if the camera is just ahead of the moving civilian line and facing back toward Tal Corvus. Use a compressed 50mm-equivalent feel so the route appears narrow and the opposing forces feel close.

PRIMARY FOCAL SHAPE: a chain of civilian transports / evacuation craft running vertically through the center from lower foreground toward the green beacon line. The craft should vary in size and condition and read as evacuation traffic, not a military formation.

ARMED MARGINS: Fleet blue/gold ships occupy one outer flank and Shard red ships the opposite flank. Keep them partially cropped by the sides so they feel like pressure squeezing the frame rather than equal protagonists.

HUMAN ANCHOR: Tess stands or is framed at the lower-left route edge, three-quarter back to camera, watching the civilian movement. She should be smaller than the route itself. Her stance is protective and alert, not victorious.

CORRIDOR PHYSICS: show a narrow verified low-tension volume centered on green beacon geometry. It is not a glowing tunnel wall. The safe route should feel like a precise path through dangerous space, not a magical portal.
WEAPON LANGUAGE: visible turrets, targeting orientation or restrained weapons-ready cues are enough. Do not fire beams across the civilian column on the cover.

TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: preserve dark upper space around the masthead. The central green route may continue behind the masthead as a faint line, but the brightest civilian/route cluster belongs below the tagline.
THUMBNAIL TEST: one thin green centerline, tiny civilian shapes on it, red pressure on one side, blue/gold pressure on the other. If Tess or any capital ship becomes the whole read, rebalance.
SPOILER CEILING: do not depict the final coalition rescue, Pike/Billie outcomes, any specific ship defection, or the last families safely arriving.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: evacuation under contested sovereignty. The image should make movement itself feel brave and precarious.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: conventional fleet battle poster; huge hero ship blocking the civilians; green portal tunnel; civilians rendered as identical military craft; Tess facing the reader with weapons; explosions that imply the outcome.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 5 Cover
summary: Sell Jex Marrin's private route knowledge colliding with public hunger: the thing that made him powerful becomes impossible to keep private when people arrive needing a way through.
settingText: Jex Marrin's route room / Veil-adjacent broker space at the moment a hungry crowd reaches the threshold; layered route boards and a door opening onto waiting civilians.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: Jex stands at the threshold between a private route map and people who need it to survive.

CAMERA / FRAMING: eye-level 40mm-equivalent view from just inside Jex's broker room looking toward the open door. Jex stands slightly off-center in the doorway, turned three-quarters toward the waiting people while the route board remains clearly visible behind him.
PRIMARY FOCAL TRIANGLE: Jex's face and hand, the route board behind him, and the first waiting civilian outside. These three points should tell the whole cover without text.

JEX PERFORMANCE: guarded, dry, accustomed to leverage. One hand rests near a physical route control, marker or slate as if he could close the system or open it. Do not make him noble, anguished or action-ready.
ROUTE BOARD: practical and specific—green verified segments, route marks, physical notes, dim private branches. No floating neon hologram cloud. No readable prose, labels or fake alien text.

CROWD: compress the people at the threshold into tired faces, ration containers, repair gear and ordinary clothing. They are waiting, not storming the room. Keep the nearest face readable and the rest subordinate.
LIGHTING: warmer practical worklight inside Jex's room, cooler market spill beyond the door. The route map provides a controlled green accent, not the dominant ambient color.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: darker ceiling/upper-wall field behind the masthead. Keep Jex's head below the tagline and the route-board glow away from the cream title edges.
THUMBNAIL TEST: one white-haired man in a doorway, luminous route map behind him, people waiting outside. If individual props disappear and the idea disappears with them, simplify.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show Jex giving all routes away, the later public distribution method, or any downstream attack caused by the route information.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: information becoming a moral resource. The visual question is whether Jex keeps owning the road once survival depends on sharing it.
FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: cyberpunk hacker pose; wall of unreadable holograms; angry mob; Jex smiling benevolently; treasure/money symbolism; route board so bright it becomes magical.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 6 Cover
summary: Sell the instant Abby Saville's allegiance becomes a decision rather than a label: the Triarch has ordered civilian traffic stopped, the next crossing is open, and Abby is expected to enforce it.
settingText: Shard command bridge overlooking Auric Gate as a civilian convoy approaches a verified green crossing under armed Shard observation.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: Abby has a clean order to stop civilian traffic, a clean firing solution, and enough time to decide whether she will obey.

CAMERA / FRAMING: close-medium 50mm-equivalent bridge portrait. Abby fills the lower-right third from chest up in sharp three-quarter profile. Her near hand rests on or just above a weapons / command control surface in the lower foreground. The crossing remains visible over her shoulder.
EYE LINE: Abby looks past the controls toward the convoy, not at the reader and not down at her hand. Her face should communicate calculation and ownership of the decision, not confusion.

BACKGROUND STORY: outside the bridge, small civilian craft enter the verified green Auric Gate lane. Their scale must make them visibly vulnerable. Red Shard weapon readiness or targeting geometry can frame the lane but must not become a literal red beacon state.
CONTROL SURFACE: readable as weapons/command hardware through shape and light only. No legible order text, no giant 'FIRE' button, no melodramatic finger hovering over a trigger.
LIGHTING: practical Shard bridge darkness with bright-red instrumentation accents; green lane reflections lightly touch the canopy or console, not a symbolic split-light across Abby's face.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: keep Abby's head and the civilian lane below the tagline. The top quarter stays structurally quiet and dark enough for the Issue 1 masthead system.
THUMBNAIL TEST: Abby profile + one hand at the control + one green civilian line under red threat. If the bridge background reads as generic cockpit clutter, remove it.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show Abby's refusal, captains siding with her, the crossing succeeding, or the Triarch losing control.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: disobedience before it happens. The cover must preserve the possibility that Abby could still carry out the order.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: Abby already pulling her hand away; obvious moral halo; split-face red/green poster cliché; Triarch portrait looming behind her; battle already underway; civilians too small to register.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 7 Cover
summary: Sell the Calm Corridor's impossible physics before anyone understands the solution: a perfectly ordered convoy sees an equally perfect duplicate where no second convoy can exist.
settingText: Inside the apparently calm corridor: clean low-tension geometry, ordered convoy formation, impossible duplicate convoy offset in physically wrong space, stars beginning to misregister.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: a convoy sees an exact second version of itself occupying impossible space.

CAMERA / FRAMING: exterior long-lens portrait composition with the convoy traveling diagonally from lower-left toward upper-right beneath the masthead. A second materially identical convoy occupies a displaced parallel path where no second route exists.

FALSE MIRROR LOGIC: do not use a literal center mirror line. Instead, make one featured ship and its duplicate unmistakably identical in hull orientation, running lights and damage marks, while background stars and beacon positions fail to agree between the two spatial readings.

SPATIAL WRONGNESS: the duplicate should be too close / too coincident for the apparent depth. One ship can partially occlude geometry that says it should be behind something else. The contradiction must be geometric, not spectral.
MATERIALITY: both versions are fully solid and equally illuminated. No transparency, glow-ghost effect, motion blur apparition, fog silhouette or magical reflection.
CORRIDOR STATE: calm, verified green beacons and clean low-tension geometry make the impossible duplication more disturbing. Do not pre-signal danger with a red corridor.
ANOMALY COLOR: Warp Black depth, Ion White and subtle Plasma Violet refraction only where geometry misregisters. Fleet blue/gold/white and Verge/convoy colors stay normal.

TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: keep the masthead on clean dark space; allow only sparse stars behind it. The paired convoy silhouettes should begin below the tagline so the identical pattern survives at thumbnail size.
THUMBNAIL TEST: two clearly identical formations. The wrongness must be visible before any fine anomaly detail.
SPOILER CEILING: do not reveal that breaking formation helps, do not show manual-control escape vectors, and do not depict the convoy already clear of the anomaly.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: hard-SF uncertainty. The first reaction should be 'Why are there two of them?' not 'What monster is that?'

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: kaleidoscope; wormhole; literal mirror glass; ghost ships; blue-purple psychedelic tunnel; abstract geometry with no recognizable convoy; different ships that merely resemble each other.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 8 Cover
summary: Sell the Shard challenge as politics compressed into a ritual circle: Tess Banks and Oren Pike face one another before the watching network, with command legitimacy reduced to the length of a blade.
settingText: Shard challenge circle / arena under hard practical light; ring of captains and observers, Tessa Banks and Oren Pike facing each other before the first decisive exchange.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: two people inside a circle, an entire political order waiting on what happens between them.

CAMERA / FRAMING: low 32–35mm-equivalent view from just outside the arena boundary, camera roughly knee-to-waist height. Tess stands left-middle and Pike right-middle, separated by a large charged area of empty floor. Their full silhouettes must remain readable.

CIRCLE GEOMETRY: the arena boundary should curve strongly through the lower frame and wrap behind them, visually trapping the confrontation. The watching captains occupy a dark ring beyond, not a cheering crowd.
TESS PERFORMANCE: balanced stance, shoulders quiet, blade low or ready but not brandished. Her body says she will fight if required but refuses to perform rage for the audience.
PIKE PERFORMANCE: weight forward, more open blade presentation, attention fixed on Tess. He wants the ritual to become spectacle without becoming a cartoon berserker.
WEAPONS: practical Shard blades with established materials. No oversized fantasy swords, sparks, crossed blades, blood or impact moment.
LIGHTING: hard overhead white industrial light on the circle; bright-red Shard markings at boundary/control points; surrounding chamber falls into forge-adjacent darkness. Keep skin tones natural.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: upper arena architecture should form a quiet dark header field. Keep both heads below the tagline and do not let a blade intrude through the masthead.
THUMBNAIL TEST: two distinct people, one circular boundary, two small blades, one watching ring. If the crowd reads first, darken/simplify it.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show Tess winning, Pike down, Tess refusing the kill, or captains changing sides.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: legitimacy, violence and restraint. The empty space between Tess and Pike is the tension engine.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: crossed-sword duel poster; blood spray; cheering arena crowd; fantasy gladiator costumes; Tess snarling; Pike rendered as inhuman monster; result implied by who is visually dominant.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 9 Cover
summary: Sell Jex Marrin becoming the target of the very network that made him valuable: Veil Market is hungry, route knowledge and money have converged around him, and too many people now know he knows where the food went.
settingText: Veil Market at night, dense but grounded working market lanes around Jex Marrin's position; route markers, closed stalls, ration scarcity and multiple lines of attention converging on him.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: every structural line and every social glance in Veil Market has started converging on Jex.

CAMERA / FRAMING: 50mm-equivalent street portrait at eye level. Jex is mid-stride in the lower-middle of the frame, turning his head slightly over one shoulder because he has noticed the market noticing him. Do not freeze him in a pose.
CONVERGING GEOMETRY: awning edges, catwalk rails, hanging cables, route-light lines and corridor perspective should subtly point toward Jex without becoming literal arrows.

SOCIAL THREAT: place two or three ordinary market figures at different depths whose attention is clearly on Jex. None may display a weapon. The ambiguity is the hook: customer, informant, watcher, attacker?
JEX PROP: a compact route slate, ledger or physical marker is close to his body, identifiable as useful information rather than money. He should hold it protectively but not clutch it in fear.
SCARCITY: closed food shutters, depleted bins, ration containers and sparse commerce establish hunger. No riot, flames or overturned market.
LIGHTING: deep market shadow with practical white/amber worklight, muted green route accents and sparse bright-red Shard marks. Keep the palette dirty and inhabited, not neon.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: a dark awning/upper passage creates the masthead field. Keep Jex's pale hair and face below the tagline for clean silhouette separation.
THUMBNAIL TEST: one pale-haired figure isolated in a dense converging market. The viewer should feel he is singled out even if the route slate disappears at small size.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show the attempt on Jex's life, its failure, who paid for anything, his evidence release, or the Shatterforge connection.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: conspiracy pressure at human scale. Veil Market should feel like Jex's own terrain becoming hostile without visibly changing its rules.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: visible assassin with weapon; noir trench-coat cliché; cyberpunk neon bazaar; chase scene; Jex centered like an action hero; exaggerated frightened expression; literal money piles.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 10 Cover
summary: Sell Shatterforge as an engineered disaster masquerading as industrial failure: the Spire is overheating, workers are trapped, and the vents that should save them are visibly sealed.
settingText: Shatterforge industrial spire under runaway heat load; sealed vent structures glowing, workers trapped behind industrial geometry, approach path for Abby and Tess.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: an industrial system built to vent heat is visibly cooking because its relief paths are mechanically shut.

CAMERA / FRAMING: extreme low-angle 24–28mm-equivalent view up the Shatterforge vertical stack from a lower access gantry. The structure should occupy roughly two-thirds of the image height below the masthead, making Abby and Tess visibly tiny.

PRIMARY SILHOUETTE: a tall central forge spine with several large vent trunks/petals that are visibly clamped, dogged or mechanically sealed. The closed safety architecture must be understandable without labels.

HEAT STORY: white-yellow internal heat leaks through seams and vent joints; metal surfaces show thermal bloom and localized glow. Steam/smoke vents from unintended gaps. Avoid giant open flames unless physically justified by a breach.
HUMAN STAKE: tiny worker silhouettes are visible behind a protected bridge/window level inside the structure. They should read as trapped occupants, not decorative scale figures.

ABBY / TESS STAGING: Abby advances toward the hot structure on the lower gantry; Tess is several body lengths behind, following into danger. Neither faces the reader. Their relative positions must imply pursuit/rescue without revealing what happens.
COLOR: dark industrial steel and soot, white-yellow heat, restrained Shard red control markings, practical service lights. No fantasy-lava palette and no broad orange wash.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: use black smoke/dark void above the tallest vent structures as the masthead field. No bright flare behind cream masthead lettering.
THUMBNAIL TEST: one huge dark machine with glowing sealed seams and two tiny people moving toward it. If the viewer sees 'explosion' instead of 'sealed overheating system,' redesign.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show the evidence package, Abby's disappearance, any final escape, or the identity/motive behind the sabotage.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: industrial rescue plus conspiracy. The system itself is the antagonist on the cover because somebody has made it behave wrong.
FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: exploding refinery; lava volcano; Abby/Tess giant heroic foreground portraits; readable warning signs; open vents; proof/evidence visible; workers safely evacuated.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 11 Cover
summary: Sell Auric Gate at the edge of renewed war just as impossible Rift duplicates make targeting itself untrustworthy: everybody has a target until nobody can be sure what they are aiming at.
settingText: Auric Gate standoff in open space: Fleet and Shard formations facing one another, weapon locks active, a physically impossible duplicate ship appearing between or overlapping the lines, stressed corridor geometry.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: two armed formations have perfect reasons to fire, and a materially real ship that should not exist has appeared exactly in the shared target space.

CAMERA / FRAMING: long-lens exterior portrait view compressed along the confrontation axis. Fleet ships enter from the left/lower-left, Shard ships from the right/lower-right, leaving a narrow central vertical void beneath Auric Gate geometry.

CENTRAL IMPOSSIBILITY: place one ship in the contested center and an impossible duplicate of that same exact hull partly displaced through the same target space. The two must share distinctive silhouette and markings so the duplication is unmistakable.

TARGET READINESS: gun orientation, opening weapons ports, restrained targeting lights and formation posture establish that both sides are ready. Do not show fired beams, muzzle flashes, missiles in flight or impact.

DUPLICATE MATERIALITY: both copies are fully opaque, physically lit and equally plausible. Their contradiction is position, not ghost effect. One may occlude a pylon or ship in a way that makes the depth impossible.
AURIC GATE: retain recognizable pylon and crossing-lane geography behind the standoff so this is the same civic infrastructure previously used for movement, now turned into a battlefield.
ANOMALY COLOR: Ion White / restrained violet spatial stress around the duplicated geometry only; no giant portal. Fleet blue/gold and Shard red remain clearly separate.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: upper Warp Black field remains quiet for masthead. Do not put the brightest anomaly flare behind the title. The central duplicated hull should start below the tagline.
THUMBNAIL TEST: blue/gold armed mass left, red armed mass right, one impossible repeated ship between them. If the duplication is not obvious small, simplify the fleet count.
SPOILER CEILING: do not show weapons being lowered, the Mirror Star collapsing, Billie stopping Pike, or the battle's final de-escalation.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: brinkmanship under epistemic failure. The cover is about the danger of acting before certainty returns.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: active broadside; giant explosion; translucent ghost ship; generic portal; too many ships to read the duplicate; one faction visually framed as obviously villainous; de-escalation already visible.

title: Rex Fleet Issue 12 Cover
summary: Sell the first Shattered Accord as the harder work after the guns stop: people who were shooting at one another yesterday have to write rules today because another convoy is already coming.
settingText: Functional negotiation room overlooking Auric Gate; unsigned agreement centered on a table, Fleet/Verge/Shard representatives around it, next civilian convoy visible approaching the green crossing beyond the window.
panelPlan: ONE DOMINANT COVER IDEA: the next convoy is already approaching while people who were shooting at one another yesterday still have an unsigned set of rules between them.

CAMERA / FRAMING: 35mm-equivalent view from slightly above table height, angled toward a large window overlooking Auric Gate. The unsigned agreement occupies the lower-center foreground; participants form a broken arc around it; the incoming convoy sits in the distance beyond the glass.

PRIMARY FOCAL OBJECT: the paper / document is centered enough to register but must not contain readable body text. It is visibly incomplete through blank signature lines, separated signing fields or an uncapped stylus nearby—never through giant words such as 'UNSIGNED.'

HANDS / FACTIONS: four distinct sets of hands and sleeves approach the table edge from different sides. Fleet blue/gold/white, Verge green/practical civilian language and Shard red/industrial materials remain visibly separate. No hands touch each other.

FACES: Venn, Naomi, Tess and Billie may be visible above/around the table, but none gets a heroic center portrait. Eyelines should cross toward the document or one another, creating active disagreement rather than solemn posing.
OUTSIDE DEADLINE: through the window, a small civilian convoy is already approaching the verified green Auric Gate route. It should be visible enough to read as movement, not scenic background.
AFTERMATH: subtle scars on the Gate, distant damaged infrastructure or holstered gear can remind us of the prior fight. No active weapons in hands, no celebratory cleanup.
LIGHTING: neutral practical negotiation-room light; cooler space/window light beyond; distinct faction colors remain accents. Do not blend everyone into a warm unity glow.
TRADE-DRESS COMPOSITION: the window's upper dark space creates the masthead field. Keep all faces below the tagline and keep the convoy away from the issue-number block.
THUMBNAIL TEST: one pale unsigned document, incompatible hands around it, one approaching green-route convoy beyond. If the faces become the main read, pull the camera back or lower them.
SPOILER CEILING: do not reveal the Accord's final terms, who signs, whether anyone gains command authority, or the final editorial return message.

directionInline.text: EMOTIONAL PROMISE: governance as suspense. The visual deadline is outside the window; the unresolved mechanism is on the table.

FAILURE MODES TO REJECT: handshake; signatures already present; smiling unity portrait; conference-room stock-photo composition; one faction chairing the table like obvious victor; readable legal prose; celebratory sunrise glow.
